questions: Why did late acquisition fall to roughly 12-13 lanes per hour?
Which algorithms and G x N x F load cells produced long process-wall tails?
Can slow lanes be attributed to measured workload compute, Unity startup/finalization, inter-process gaps, or only described as an order-associated drift?
Which frozen ST workloads are structurally excessive for practical formal collection?
Why did the original full validator take excessively long and consume excessive memory?

quantiles.method: linear interpolation equivalent to Python statistics.quantiles inclusive endpoints via explicit p*(n-1) indexing
quantiles.missingRule: do not impute missing timestamps or workload boundaries

tailRules.pooledTailThreshold: pooled valid lane process-wall P95 frozen after reading only the validated timing vector
tailRules.orderStrata: ordinal-based early/middle/late thirds, fixed before identity disclosure
tailRules.smallCellRule: for low-n algorithm x G x N x F cells report n, min, median, max; do not present P99 as a stable population estimate

timeDecomposition.startup: workloadStartUtc - processCreateUtc only if a trustworthy explicit boundary exists
timeDecomposition.compute: workloadEndUtc - workloadStartUtc only if trustworthy explicit boundaries exist
timeDecomposition.finalization: processExitUtc - workloadEndUtc only if a trustworthy explicit boundary exists

causalBoundary: Order drift and correlations are descriptive. Thermal throttling, cache, antivirus, disk, or memory pressure are supported causes only with direct structural evidence; otherwise they remain candidate explanations.
scientificBoundary: This is post-qualification engineering diagnosis, not formal algorithm-effect analysis and not authority to alter the scientific design.
